name: Acrylic Phase Bass
description: After Howard Scarr's tutorial for the instrument: the notch bass hard-clipped, its sweep quicker, the mids lifted and a phaser turning through it.

name: Banded Detune Bass
description: After a thread on the Dogs On Acid forum: three detuned saws through a band-pass and a notch, a synced LFO turning the cutoff in half notes: a dark, phasing drum-and-bass growl.

name: Glide Acid Line
description: After a thread on the maker's forum about acid lines: one saw through the three-pole filter, resonant, accented by velocity, gliding where notes touch, warmed below and echoed in quarters.

name: Rectifier Wah Bass
description: After Howard Scarr's tutorial for the instrument: the squelch bass with its filter as a notch that sweeps in slowly, through the rectifier at full: a funky, wah-like growl.

name: Rolling Night Bass
description: After a full-on bassline thread on the psynews forum: a saw and a synced saw a fourth below through the four-pole filter, short and tight with a little drive, for rolling sixteenth lines.

name: Squelch Club Bass
description: After Howard Scarr's tutorial for the instrument: synced saws over a full sub, the analog boost and punch up, a resonant filter that squelches, its decay shortening the harder it opens.

name: Thunk Saw Bass
description: After a thread on the Elektronauts forum: two saws between a shut low-pass and a high-pass, a synced saw LFO knocking the cutoff open in dotted sixteenths and a slow sine wandering under it.

name: Hyper Rave Stab
description: After Chromatic's drum-and-bass stab walkthrough in Computer Music: saw stacks an octave apart over a low saw, twin unison and hard distortion, a synced LFO moving the mix, all three pitches bent up a fifth by an envelope, through the doppler tape echo.

name: Contour Dive
description: After Howard Scarr's tutorial for the instrument: a one-shot saw LFO dropping the first oscillator from an octave up into pitch at every note, against the steady second: a falling, laser-like dive.

name: Talking Psy Buzz
description: After a psytrance effects thread on the maker's forum: a saw whose pitch flicks at each note, filtered by velocity, then the vowel filter wandering on an LFO into a long tape echo.

name: Dusty Rave Lead
description: After Howard Scarr's tutorial for the instrument: two saws in six-voice unison detuned to the limit, through the low-pass distortion, the wheel cleaning it up.

name: Eight-Voice Unison Lead
description: After the First Steps chapter of Howard Scarr's manual for the instrument: two saws stacked eight voices deep, detuned as far as they go and spread across the stereo field, a dotted echo behind, the wheel bringing in vibrato.

name: Formant Pulse Solo
description: After Richard Leon's masterclass in Sound On Sound: a thin pulse through two resonant band-passes in parallel, set apart like a voice's formants, gliding, with a vibrato that fades in.

name: Full-Suction Unison Lead
description: After the First Steps chapter of Howard Scarr's manual: the eight-voice saw stack with a sub, a little noise and a third saw an octave down, through a short dotted echo; sweep the cutoff while it plays.

name: Narrow Pulse Dive
description: After Howard Scarr's tutorial for the instrument: two thin pulses, band-passed and driven hard, a fast LFO shaking their widths under thick chorus; the wheel makes each note dive two octaves.

name: Nine-Saw Lead
description: After the First Steps chapter of Howard Scarr's manual: one oscillator as a stack of nine saws spread wide, with its sub, the filter shut and thrown open by its envelope; four unison voices, chorus and a dotted echo spread it.

name: Pressure Glide Lead
description: After the First Steps chapter of Howard Scarr's manual: a gliding mono saw lead, the wheel speeding the vibrato and the key's pressure opening the filter.

name: Rectified Solo Lead
description: After Howard Scarr's tutorial for the instrument: two saws pushed hard into the saturation, the filter envelope stretching its own attack for a swelling front, bends snapping with no smoothing.

name: Rising Sync Lead
description: After Richard Leon's masterclass in Sound On Sound: the second oscillator alone, synced to the first and swept up by the filter envelope at each note, driven a little: a tearing sync lead.

name: Twin-Saw Bright Top Lead
description: After a thread on the infekted.org forum about a saw-stack lead on the older model: three detuned voices kept fairly narrow, the second filter unlinked and resonant over the first, a phaser on top.

name: Uplift Stack Lead
description: After ADSR Sounds' trance lead walkthrough for the instrument: both oscillators as saw stacks a fifth apart, a third saw and the sub under them, twin unison, a touch of distortion, then echo and a hall.

name: Chord Gate Saw Pad
description: After Sound Design Tutorials' trance-gate video: both oscillators as saw stacks over a pulse an octave down, the arpeggiator's chord mode chopping held chords in sixteenths with a rest every third step, then chorus, the widener, echo and a hall.

name: Gated Fifths PWM Pad
description: After Richard Leon's masterclass in Sound On Sound: two pulses a fifth apart, each gated by its own square LFO pushing its width to silence, one in eighths and one in sixteenths.

name: Matrix Gate Pad
description: After a thread on the maker's forum about trance gates: the arpeggiator's steps sent through the matrix to the cutoff, so a pattern of loud and silent steps opens and shuts a detuned saw pad.

name: Quarter Pump Pad
description: After a thread on the maker's forum about pumping pads: one LFO, a rising ramp locked to quarter notes, lifts the oscillators' volume from low on every beat, as a kick's side-chain would.

name: Rectified Saw Pluck
description: After ADSR Sounds' trance pluck walkthrough, with tips from the maker's forum: a seven-saw stack, the filter snapped open and shut, four unison voices, the rectifier at full, then ping-pong echo and a hall.

name: Dirty Dotted Pluck
description: After Howard Scarr's tutorial for the instrument: the same plucked saws arpeggiated into the reverb's feedback mode, a darker, dirtier dotted echo.

name: Dotted Echo Arp
description: After Howard Scarr's tutorial for the instrument: a plucked saw pair, brighter up the keyboard, arpeggiated over two octaves into a long dotted-eighth echo whose time wavers.

name: Envelope-LFO Arp Pluck
description: After a tips thread on the Elektronauts forum: both filters shut, a one-shot falling LFO plucking them open on every arpeggiator step, through the tape echo and a light phaser.

name: Theory Strings
description: After Howard Scarr's tutorial for the instrument: two pulses with vibratos of opposite sign, a slow pan, a softer bow the harder you play, and the equalizer lifting lows, mids and highs; no chorus.
